title: SGit API — Reference Vault
tagline: A conformance target: if you can read this, every byte you needed was a plain GET of a computed path, decrypted where you are. The host that served it cannot read it.

claims.title: Names are computed, never listed
claims.note: Every object this page needed — ref, index, commit, tree, blob — has a name derived from the read key or a content hash. No listing or discovery call exists to depend on.

claims.title: Reads are plain GETs
claims.note: The read path is a sequence of GETs of deterministic paths. A static file host serves them unchanged; the live API and GitHub Pages are interchangeable for reading.

claims.title: Decryption happens client-side
claims.note: AES-256-GCM in the browser or CLI. The store — S3, Lambda, GitHub Pages, or a git repository — only ever holds ciphertext under opaque ids.

claims.title: Batch reads break on static
claims.note: A batch is a POST carrying a list of ids. The CLI's clone depends on it today; the browser transport already fans out to parallel GETs. The gap is pinned by a test that will flip when the CLI ships static fan-out.

claims.title: Writes break on static
claims.note: A published vault is a read-only snapshot. A write attempt is refused — there is nothing to accept it, and that is the point rather than a limitation.

claims.title: Authentication breaks on static
claims.note: There is no access decision left for a server to make: the read key is the whole credential, published deliberately, and the ciphertext is the protection.
